name: unbrowse
description: Use websites through the Unbrowse node on this machine: the site's own JSON, with no browser once a route is learned. WebFetch is answered from the node's routes, each node answer shows what it cost and the tokens it saved, and learned routes become tools.

agent.title: Agent
agent.description: Which agent key Claude uses: its number (`unbrowse agent new <name>` prints it; the window shows it under Money, Agents), or first for the key the node made on its first run. Let it in once with `unbrowse grant first` (or `unbrowse grant <number>`): the node asks you. No token is kept here.

web_fetch.title: WebFetch
web_fetch.description: routes (the default): when Claude fetches a page, the node answers first from a route it already has, with no browser and nothing paid, and Claude reads the site's own JSON; when it has none, WebFetch runs as usual. off: WebFetch always runs as usual.

savings.title: Tokens saved
savings.description: measure (the default): after a node answer, fetch the page it stood for once, so the receipt and the ledger can say how many tokens Claude did not read (page against answer, about four characters a token). off: no fetch, no savings figure.

route_tools.title: Route tools
route_tools.description: on (the default): each of the node's local read routes becomes a tool Claude can call (route_<site>_<what>, found with ToolSearch), and the system prompt names the sites they cover. off: neither.

heal.title: Heal routes
heal.description: on: when a route fails, the node learns the page afresh in the background (it may open its browser; it pays nothing) and a toast says how it went. off (the default): Claude decides.
